chunks.text: In October 2026, staff and local people celebrated at an Ebola clinic in the Democratic Republic of Congo, a country in central Africa. The clinic's last [[confirmed patients]] had just left. Ebola, a rare, [[deadly disease]] caused by a virus, {{broke out}} again in May. In other parts of Congo, the number of [[cases]] keeps {{going up}}. By October 31, Congo's [[health ministry]] had counted more than 5,000 deaths.

verbs.why: Fires often break out in dry weather. Fights sometimes break out at hockey games. Ebola broke out again in May.

verbs.wrong: To be checked a second time
verbs.why: Rents go up every year. The number of tourists goes up in the summer. In other parts of Congo, the number of cases keeps going up.

chunks.text: The ministry says 10,351 people have {{come down with}} Ebola. Of those, 5,026 have died and 2,788 have {{pulled through}}. Health officials call this [[outbreak]], a sudden rise of a disease, the deadliest in Congo's history. The United Nations says it is the second largest ever, after West Africa's outbreak of 2014 to 2016. Cases have also {{shown up}} in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

verbs.correct: To become sick with a disease
verbs.wrong: To nurse a person who is sick
verbs.why: Many children come down with colds in the winter. My father comes down with the flu almost every year. The ministry says 10,351 people have come down with Ebola.

verbs.correct: To stay alive after a serious illness
verbs.wrong: To leave a clinic without a test
verbs.why: Most patients pull through after this kind of surgery. Healthy adults usually pull through a bad case of the flu. The health ministry says 2,788 people have pulled through.

verbs.wrong: To end after a short time
verbs.why: Flu cases show up in our town every winter. New cases of measles sometimes show up in schools. Ebola cases have also shown up in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.

chunks.text: A rare type of the virus is behind this outbreak. It has no [[approved]] treatment or vaccine, a medicine that teaches the body to fight a disease. Several problems {{hold back}} the work against Ebola. Fighting between the government and [[armed groups]] limits where health workers can go in eastern Congo. Officials [[struggle]] to {{track down}} people who were near patients. Many people do not believe the [[health warnings]], and some workers have been attacked. Other workers have {{walked off}} the job over [[late pay]], which has {{shut down}} some [[treatment centers]].

verbs.correct: To slow the progress of something
verbs.wrong: To change who leads a project
verbs.why: A lack of money holds back many small schools. Bad roads hold back trade in poor areas. Several problems hold back the work against Ebola.
Police track down the driver of a stolen car with GPS. Reporters often track down people who saw an accident. Officials struggle to track down people who were near patients.

verbs.correct: To stop working as a protest
verbs.wrong: To sign a new work contract
verbs.why: Nurses sometimes walk off the job when a hospital cuts their pay. Bus drivers walk off the job when the company does not pay them. Some health workers have walked off the job over late pay.

verbs.wrong: To clean a place with soap
verbs.why: A long strike shuts down the factory. Heavy snow shuts down the schools in our town. The workers' strikes have shut down some treatment centers.

chunks.text: There are [[signs of progress]]. The World Health Organization says testing and treatment have grown. A [[clinical trial]], a careful test of a medicine on [[volunteers]], {{kicked off}} in eastern Congo on October 23. Doctors are giving an [[existing]] Ebola vaccine to people who were near patients. They want to {{find out}} whether it protects against this type. The organization says teams must {{step up}} their work and {{reach out}} to [[communities]] to [[build trust]].

verbs.correct: To begin an event or activity
verbs.wrong: To be approved by the government
verbs.why: The school year kicks off in September. The town festival kicks off with a big parade. A clinical trial kicked off in eastern Congo on October 23.

verbs.correct: To learn a fact you did not know
verbs.wrong: To make a new medicine in a lab
verbs.why: Students find out their grades online. Many people find out the news from their phones. Doctors want to find out whether the vaccine protects against this rare type.

verbs.wrong: To check how work was done
verbs.why: Police step up patrols before big games. Stores step up hiring before Christmas. The World Health Organization says teams must step up their work.

verbs.correct: To contact people and offer help
verbs.wrong: To collect money for a hospital
verbs.why: Good teachers reach out to parents who need help. The library reaches out to new families in town. The World Health Organization says teams must reach out to communities to build trust.

mainIdea.s: More than 5,000 people have died of Ebola in Congo since May, in what officials call its worst outbreak. Fighting and late pay make the work harder, yet thousands recovered and a vaccine trial began.
mainIdea.why: The ministry counts more than 5,000 deaths, and several problems hold back the work. Still, 2,788 people have pulled through, and a clinical trial kicked off on October 23.

mainIdea.s: A new vaccine made for this rare type of Ebola is now ending the crisis in Congo after thousands of deaths. Clinics across the east are empty, so health workers may soon move to other countries.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the trial only kicked off in October, and doctors still want to find out if the vaccine works. In other parts of Congo, the number of cases keeps going up.

mainIdea.s: Congo has opened a large children's hospital in its capital city after years of delay. Officials say doctors from Kenya and Nigeria will train local nurses there during the next two years of the plan.
mainIdea.why: This is about Ebola deaths in Congo passing 5,000. It also covers the problems that hold back the work and the vaccine trial that kicked off.

lines.text: Did you see the Ebola news from Congo? Deaths have passed 5,000.
I saw that. It's a sad story, [[to say the least]]. How many people have {{come down with}} it?
More than 10,000 since May. Cases have also {{shown up}} in Kenya, Nigeria and Uganda.
Why is it so hard to stop?
Several things {{hold back}} the work. There's fighting in eastern Congo, so health workers can't go everywhere.
[[Not to mention]] that many people don't believe the health warnings. I read about that.
Right. And officials struggle to {{track down}} people who were near patients.
Are the health workers at least getting paid?
Not always. Some have {{walked off the job}} over late pay, and that has {{shut down}} some treatment centers.
That's terrible. Is there [[a bright spot]] in all this?
Yes. Thousands of people have {{pulled through}}. And one clinic celebrated when its last confirmed patients left.
That must be [[a weight off their shoulders]]. What about a vaccine?
A trial {{kicked off}} on October 23. Doctors want to {{find out}} if an existing vaccine works against this rare type.
So can't they just give it to everyone?
[[It's not that simple]]. They don't know yet if it protects people, and the number of cases keeps {{going up}}.
So what has to happen next?
The World Health Organization says teams must {{step up}} their work and {{reach out}} to communities.
That makes me a little hopeful. Those health workers have a very hard job.

expressions.def: Used to say that the real situation is even stronger than your words
ex: The drive home was slow, to say the least.
Her first day at work was hard, to say the least.

expressions.def: Used to add one more fact that makes your point stronger
ex: The hotel was expensive, not to mention far from the beach.

expressions.def: Something good in a situation that is mostly bad
ex: The new park was a bright spot in a hard year for the town.

expressions.def: Used to say that a big worry has ended for some people
ex: They paid the last of the loan. That was a weight off their shoulders.

expressions.def: Used to say that a problem is harder than it seems
ex: He says I should just quit, but it's not that simple.
